utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Robinson, I was told that you have something to raise before we begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. Actually, I'd let Dr. Karadzic speak to this, but he's not well today and not able to proceed, and we'll be asking the Chamber to adjourn for the day because of his health situation. But I would like to ask him to explain that directly to the Chamber in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And bring in the witness. I'd like to note for the record the accused is not feeling well today. He has kindly agreed to proceed with the first witness, and the Chamber appreciates it very much. And the Chamber asks the Registry to look into the matter with the greatest care. And also I have to note that Mr. Karadzic agrees to let us know if he does not feel well in the middle of his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Soja. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: My name is Milomir Soja.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Soja, you testified in the trial against Dragomir Milosevic on the 24th and 25th of April, 2007; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review this testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you affirm that the testimony accurately reflects the evidence you provided to the Tribunal in 2007?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Soja, would you provide the same evidence to the Court if questioned on the same matters here today?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this testimony as 65 ter 22611 for admission under Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1633, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I would now read a brief summary of the witness's evidence as admitted. The witness is an electrical engineer. Before the outbreak of the war, Mr. Soja was employed by Energoinvest, in its power electronics department. The witness was mobilised at the outbreak of the war in 1992. After his release from the armed forces in December 1994, he took up his work obligation in the company Energoinvest Automatika in Ilidza. In the spring of 1995, Mr. Soja and one of his colleagues were asked to go to the Pretis ammunition factory in Vogosca, Sarajevo, regarding the modification of the ignition system for air-bomb launchers. They were accompanied by an officer from the Ilidza Brigade of the VRS. At Pretis, Mr. Soja met Major Krsmanovic, another officer of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. From Krsmanovic, the witness heard that at that time, in addition to the launcher of the Ilidza Brigade, there were two functional air-bomb launchers, one in Vogosca and the other in Ilijas. Mr. Soja subsequently learned that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps also had an air-bomb launcher in Blazuj. Major Krsmanovic was opposed to the modification of the launchers, since this would have rendered the equipment less reliable. However, the witness was asked to perform modifications using electronic components as the Ilidza Brigade intended to use this new system on their air-bomb launcher. The manufacturing of the new ignition system lasted until early summer 1995. On several occasions, the witness had to attend to a malfunctioning air-bomb launcher. In the summer of 1995, the witness was requested to attend the launching of an air-bomb targeting the cold storage plant in Stup from a launcher positioned under the overpass of Kasindolska Street, close to the witness's work-place. From this cold storage plant, the Bosnian government forces used to fire with small arms into VRS-controlled territory. The first attempted launch failed. That same evening, the witness observed the launch of the air-bomb from a distance of about 150 metres. The air-bomb did not reach the cold storage plant, but exploded prematurely on territory under the control of the VRS. During the relevant time, Mr. Soja heard the launching and detonation of the air-bombs about five to six times. There is a characteristic sound connected with the launching and detonation of air-bombs. Your Honour, this concludes the summary, and I have no further questions and I have also no associated exhibits to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Soja.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to thank you about meeting the Defence, and I believe that that fact will speed the cross-examination along. I would like to start with those things that we agreed about during our interview, and those are the things -- or, rather, questions to which you can answer with either yes or no. I'm going to word my questions in that way. The first question: Did we agree that you are familiar with Ilidza because that's where you grew up?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the settlements predominantly settled with Serbs were under the Serb control, and Muslim settlements were under the Muslim control? Let's not mention Hrasnica, Butmir, and Sokolovic Kolonija that were close to the Serbian settlements.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you - and you said it here - left Grbavica to go home to Osijek, a neighbourhood of Ilidza, at the moment when the tensions started rising and when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is not as much as you can say about Grbavica as you can say about Ilidza; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your interview on 24 July 2004, you stated that there was no military organisation in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: No, at the beginning of the war, there was no militarisation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You arrived in your village, therefore, and the local population had already started holding arms close to their homes in order to prevent attacks from the neighbouring Muslim villages; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the villagers guarded the village in shifts, and when your turn came, you also held guard.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, but at the beginning it was only during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that there were no line-ups, that there was no command of any kind there; it was a spontaneous organisation based on the fear of something that might happen to the village.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You helped me a lot, because I had already promoted general chaos, and you introduced another helper of his, and that's fear. Until mid-July, in your village and in Ilidza, were all your actions dictated by fear from the other side?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I can't tell you how long that lasted, whether that lasted until mid-June, and whether that was when certain elements of military organisations were first introduced. But, in any case, for the best part of that initial period, in my opinion, or at least that was my feeling, was predominantly fueled by fear and uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Serbs were not prepared because they had relied on the state and the JNA to help them and to keep the enemy at bay?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, I can speak on my behalf, and I can tell you that I was taken absolutely by surprise, and people that I spoke to felt the same. I can't speak in general terms. I can only tell you what I know and what I felt.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The word in the transcript is "the enemy," and I said "the other side." I didn't mean the enemy, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true, what you said, that the guards service and later on the front-line were only about 50 metres away from the houses, from the settlement?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: In my case in Osijek, where I resided and where I spent the first few months of the war, that was correct. The front-lines were not military lines at all. We simply held guard close to the banks of the river that surrounded our village, and the same was true throughout the war of Ilidza, which throughout the war remained either on the front-line or very close to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did we also agree that in Ilidza, itself, there were no Muslim settlements that would be under the Serb control?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also stated that the Serbs guarded the Osijek Muslims, that they visited them, and that they encouraged them and promised them that nobody would do them any harm, but they also expressed their fear that some rogue elements or renegade elements might do them harm.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that that's why some Muslims left Osijek and exchanged their property, and is it also true that the others stayed on and were treated fairly by the authorities and by their Serb neighbours?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the war, you were a reservist of the JNA, and like all the other reservists, you brought the reserve uniform home, but you did not bear any arms because your specialty was a multiple rocket-launcher.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Muslim and Serb reservists take uniforms and weapons home in peacetime when they had attended manoeuvres, and they took uniforms home and light infantry weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I am sure that that was the case with the uniform. I, myself, did not take weapons home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about gas masks?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Anything else, in terms of the equipment; the shovels or anything?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I'm not sure about shovels. There was a duffle bag with a uniform, a gas mask, eating utensils, the basic military utensils, without weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you say that people of Osijek organised themselves, and they had mortars that they positioned on the hilltops around Osijek?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I'm not sure that mortars existed before the first troops were organised. I can't tell you even the date when the whole thing grew into a military organisation. It more or less coincided with the first so-called attacks against Ilidza. I don't know when the first mortars appeared. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that every local commune, including yours, had Territorial Defence which was organised in accordance with the law, and the Territorial Defence had its weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Certainly. Each company and each local commune, according to the law, had its unit of Territorial Defence, and I suppose that the unit also had to have some kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any weapons that the factories and big companies had? And in addition to Territorial Defence units, did they also have weapons depots?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I suppose they did. I never saw them. But these units must have existed, so I suppose that there had to have been appropriate weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were personally a member of a delegation which toured the Osijek Muslims to try to relax them and to ease the tensions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The authorities did not exert any pressure against the Osijek Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: As far as I know, they did not, never.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have a look at a map. Mr. Soja could explain for us more easily, by referring to the map, a specific incident between Energoinvest and the cold storage plant. It should be best, the following section of the map. The ERN number is 0557-3368, section 9 of this map. It's a map of Sarajevo in which separation lines are also marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the 65 ter number is 09390C. And what page is it? 09390C; correct? Yes, I see the nodding of Mr. Reid. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it should actually be sheet 10, where we see an industrial complex, if that's the map that Mr. Karadzic would like to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sheet 9 or sheet 10?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sheet 10 is fine as well. If we can zoom in around the part of the city close to the TV, because Mr. Soja is familiar with this part of the city, and, allegedly, what was used there were the modified bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Soja, can you recognise here the building of the TV station?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Soja, could you wait a minute. Our usher will help you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. That is the TV station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that across the road from this building is the Geodetic Institute?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it by a smaller circle.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put number 1 next to the TV station building and number 2 next to the land survey building.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please encircle the big factory Vaso Miskin Crni?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I think that this is approximately here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it with number 3?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show us where Energoinvest was located?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, Vaso Miskin Crni is practically a part of Energoinvest, but there were some other factories that were part of the Energoinvest and they were located approximately here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that to the west of this was the distribution centre and some other plants of the Energoinvest?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please encircle this section as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It's roughly around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that there are no residential buildings in this area?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that to the right, that is to say to the east of the TV station building, is Astra and then Uniklima and some other industrial plants?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I remember that there were some other plants, and a few days ago I could recall, by looking at an appropriate map, that that was how they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please write the date and sign this map. I now wish to present a photograph of this area so that all the participants could see how this area where two modified bombs landed looked like.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Do you mean this map, where I already marked the circles?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you could just write the date and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Can you just remind me? What is today's date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 30th of September.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have it admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D674.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I wish to show a photograph of this, and then we could look at section 9 of this very same document. But now can we please see 21214, 65 ter 21214. 65 ter 21214.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: According to the Prosecution note, this is the correct 65 ter number. It's a photo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now we can see this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will ask you to mark on this photo, first of all, the TV station building.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]. This is the TV station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, just like that. Thank you. And can you now please mark the Land Survey Institute.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: The Land Survey Institute [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the police station, close to the Land Survey Institute, can you mark it as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I'm not sure where exactly was the police station, to the right or to the left. To be honest, I don't really remember. Maybe what is at the lower left-hand corner, which I marked -- I think it was part of the trolley bus plant of Astra.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please mark to the right Astra and Igman.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: It's approximately around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please mark the Vaso Miskin Crni.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So number 2 is the Land Survey Institute, number 3 is Uniklima, Astra and Igman, and number 4 is Vaso Miskin Crni, but you didn't include all of it.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, that was it, more or less. There were various factories there. I'm not sure what were all the buildings that belonged to the Vaso Miskin complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now please draw a circle from the left to the right by which you would mark the borders of the entire industrial complex.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, it would be approximately around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There, as we can see, are no residential buildings; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that parallel to the upper line there was a former Drinska Street which is now called Safeta Zajke?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I agree that there's a street there, but I didn't know what it was called nor what it is called now, but I suppose that those names are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please write the date and your initials on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see section 9 of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit D675.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. From the previous document, just section 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before it appears on the screen, Mr. Soja, we can perhaps go through what we agreed about during the interview, and we did it easily. Is it correct that for a long time, Otes was in the hands of the Muslim Army and that it -- from it, they shot at and attacked the Serbian part of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also agreed, as somebody who had served the army, that taking control of Otes was motivated by military logic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We also agreed that Serbs were in the Energoinvest complex and the Muslims in the cold storage plant complex.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did we also agree -- this is not section 9. Or maybe it is, but we just need one. Did we agree that the cold storage plant was full of troops and that it was used as a firing position and also as a military materiel depot?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was full of troops and if it was used as a military warehouse, but it's certain that fire was opened against Ilidza from it. So certainly there were troops inside occasionally. But whether it was also used as a warehouse or not, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to receive a document about that, I will ask you something else first. We can see the separation line here. Can I please ask you to encircle the Energoinvest complex and the cold storage plant complex.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: What is already encircled here -- oops, I'm sorry. [Marks]. What is already encircled here is the Energoinvest complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it with the letter E.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please encircle the cold storage plant.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [Marks]. This is approximately the cold storage plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with the letter H for "Hladnjaca"?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was the Market Street? Can you mark it, because that's where the separation line was.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I can. It is marked here already. One can see it. Should I encircle it or should I just indicate where it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe you can draw a line parallel to that street.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, this was the part of the Market Street, the Pijacna Street in B/C/S, which was parallel to the forward separation line [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it with the letters PU or PS to stand for "Pijacna Street"?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You -- that is to say, the Army of Republika Srpska launched modified bombs from Energoinvest in the direction of Hladnjaca. Was there any residential building in the space between these two complexes?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: It did not shoot them from the location of Energoinvest, but from the place across the street. That was below Kasindolska Street, below the overpass, but it is true that practically there were no residential buildings in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have heard of at least one incident of testing the precision of the modified bomb, and the testing took place in Zuca, where there are also no residential buildings but just huge military fortifications, both Muslim and Serbs ones; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You do not exclude the possibility that there were more testings, but there was at least one?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about one such testing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were called to improve the launching and to improve the ignition in order to reinforce the ignition, and that was your duty; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: They called me from the company in which I was under work obligation at the time, and I was told that a launcher should be made in the Ilidza Brigade and that for the launcher we should try to make a modification, or an improvement or something - I don't remember the formulation precisely - of the ignition system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Army of Republika Srpska, nor the OTP, asked you anything about the precision of the system of the rocket motors that existed, but just about igniting and activating these bombs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And during the interview a few days ago, did we agree that the rocket motors were the regular motors for the Grad rockets, with performances by which you could calculate the trajectory?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: When I was at the only meeting about the system, I was told, as far as I remember, that these were rocket motors which are used for anti-Hale rockets. Whether these were really rocket motors from the anti-Hale rockets or some other type of rocket motors is something that I could not confirm. What I can state as my opinion is certainly that whatever kind of motors was used, it couldn't be improvised. These had to be some of the existing rocket motors which are used for some sort of purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And such motors, as a rule, have specific performances and tables for targeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, I suppose they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In one of the statements, you mentioned that you had heard that one of those modified air bombs had been used against Visoko. Was it used against civilian targets; did you know that or did you not know?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I did not have any information as to what was targeted. I learnt it only by chance, because the launcher that we worked on had failed during the launching, and while we were trying to remove that, I was told that a bomb had been launched against Visoko, but I didn't know anything about the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had about 60 to -- 40- to 60-kilometre-long front-line in the city and around 250 in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you about the kilometres, but the fact is that the front-line was, indeed, very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In one of your statements, you stated that you had never heard any of the modified bombs having been used against civilians.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about targets. Where I moved about and where I resided is a valley, so it was impossible to see where those bombs and other bombs were falling. You could hear detonations coming from certain directions, but I didn't have any information about possible targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We also mentioned Stupsko Brdo and Stupska Petlja? Who controlled Stupsko Brdo and Stupska Petlja throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Either Muslims or Muslim and Croat forces together. In any case, it wasn't the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. I have to wait for the transcript. We speak the same language, and our interpreters are experiencing problems with the two of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, could you kindly put the date and your signature on this map, and we'll keep it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be D676.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We agreed that due to the sanctions in 1995, when those bombs were modified and sanctions were imposed on Yugoslavia and Serbia by the entire world, there was a shortage of ammunition and other equipment in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard, and I believe that it was, indeed, the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In one of your statements, you were asked about Vlasi [phoen] Vidovic, whom you didn't know, but you were familiar with his nickname, Vaske. So you didn't know him under his name?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you said that it was a very unconventional [as interpreted] unit in Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you also said, on cross-examination in the General Milosevic case on 25 April 2007, that you had never heard of any crimes that he may have committed.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear of any crimes that he had committed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript, it says "very unconventional," and I said "one unconventional unit." I just want to make those slight corrections for the transcript. I would like to call up a document, 1D2431.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You will help us with this. This is a document issued by the Muslim 102nd Motorised Brigade. Do you agree that the area around the cold storage plant was under its control?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the name of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In any case, the Muslim Army was present there all the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2431.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will not read all of it; just the parts that have been translated. I'm going to read for you. The Command of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, strictly confidential, 9th of November, 1993: "On the basis of the need, and in an effort to do as good and effective work and safety of persons that are residing in the cold storage plant, the 1st Motorised Battalion, the 2nd Motorised Battalion, Light Artillery Rocket Battalion of the Anti-Aircraft Defence, and in an effort to establish functionality of this facility for carrying out combat actions, I hereby order ..." And there are ten items on the first page and they are all relative to the modification of the cold storage plant so that it could be used in combat. Does this sound convincing? Does this document sound convincing?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Please allow me to read everything. It does sound convincing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there another cold storage plant in the area or is this the only one?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: This is the only one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could I tender this document into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification, pending full translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D677, Your Honours, MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2391 is the next document I would like to call up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the heading, where it says "The Command of the 102nd Motorised Brigade." 800 hours, the 1st of February, 1994, and this is an order for the usage of artillery in defence, the section of the map, and so on and so forth, the general area of Stup. Is Stup the place where both Energoinvest and the cold storage plant were located?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, approximately, although I would say that the cold storage plant also occupies one part of Azici, although it was always popularly known as the cold storage plant in Stup. And Energoinvest was also known as a facility in Stup.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have to be mindful of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under item 1, it says: "The enemy --" which means the Serbs in this case; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "In previous combat actions, the enemy has gained control over the wider area of Doglodi village, Otes, Kasindolska Street, Nedzarici village, and they have reached the following line: The Miljacka River by the Spajic farm, the Elektro-shop, the Vidic house, the Market Street, the Dobrinja River, the flower shop, the Nedzarici Barracks, the red house, the Nedzarici Elementary school, and they have organised their defence with an intention to continue combat activities." Under 2, it says: "The 102nd Motorised Brigade is organising decisive defence in the area of Sentrotrans, including the old pensioners' home, the Zora factory and Sipad ..." And so on and so forth. Further down, it says: "Observation point 01 at the cold storage plant and observation point 2 is taken by the Mixed Artillery Battalion. The command post in the Halilovic sector, the Magros facility." Can we please move on to the following page in the Serbian language. Under 5, let's not read everything, but it says: "The anti-armour fight focused on the axis: Azici-Stup, Pijacna Street, the cold storage plant, Kasindolska Street --"

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we also have the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you can read them later on. Just put your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This deployment of forces, is that what you were familiar with, and does this speak about continuous urban fighting in this part of Ilidza, Mr. Soja?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the Muslim side, there was artillery, there were anti-armour tools, and that the cold storage plant is in the center of all those combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's not go on reading. Everybody can read for themselves. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: As with the previous document, the accused just uses the term "the storage plant," that's mentioned in here, although -- and it has nothing to do with the evidence of the witness. This first -- this last document that was marked for identification is from 1993. It is a document from the Muslim forces. And here in this here is again a document from the Muslim forces from 1994 that has nothing to do with the evidence of the witness. I don't -- I object to that to be admitted just on the fact that the witness is familiar, in general terms, with the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the accused not entitled to put questions about his case to the witness, who is familiar with the case?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour, but I just object against admitting of the document. That was my observation. There is no foundation for admitting this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness testifies about the attempts of destruction of the cold storage plant in 1995. However, the pretext or the cause for that action was permanent fighting from the very outset of the war. During all this time, the cold storage plant was in the center of all the events. And the witness knows very well the line never moved in that area, that the Muslims were in the cold storage plant all the time, and there was shooting coming from the cold storage plant all the time. And this document shows what the witness knows already; that the fire coming from the cold storage plant came from the anti-armour pieces, from infantry weapons, and that it was a focal point of combat throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is no doubt that the cold storage plant was used for military purposes. But this document is actually about fighting in other areas as well, and the witness has not provided any knowledge of fighting in certain areas that are mentioned here. He's concerned with the cold storage plant and not all these other areas.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond again? One witness was here and said that Stup was controlled by the Serbs, and this witness knows that the situation was just the contrary, it was under the Muslim control, and Stupsko Brdo and Stupska Petlja were always under the Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We do not think the Prosecution is challenging the authenticity of this document, and the witness was able to confirm the part of this document, which is of only three pages. We don't think there's any problem in admitting this. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D678, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. 1D2340 [as interpreted] is the next document I would like to call up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not 243 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2430. That's not the document. 1D2430, another document issued by the 102nd Muslim Brigade. Yes, that's the document. We're not going to read all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you, Mr. Soja, and you can very well see it next to the number 30/2, the enemy is grouped in Doglodi, Kasindolska, Nedzarici, and the enemy has engaged troops to hold the lines. Do you agree with their estimate, that the Serbs had to engage senior troops to man the line?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it due to the fact that the Muslim side over-powered the Serbs, in terms of the number of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on to the following page, item 3. I believe that we can stay on the same page in English. Or, rather, we need item 4, I decided. Can we move on to the following page in English as well, the part that begins: "I decided ..." I don't know if there's a translation in English. It says: "I decided ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you follow, sir: "I decided to organise a decisive defence in the area of responsibility at the present positions with the focus being on the axis: Ilidza, Kasindolska Street, Nedzarici, [indiscernible], the cold storage plant, the Stupska Petlja ..." And so on and so forth. Is it true that the lines were very close to each other throughout the war in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not have the English translation of all the items. We just have some of them translated. Could we please see, after this, two pages on, the fourth page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And here, on top of the page, it says: "Stup-Energoinvest, Stup-Otes, Stup-Doglodi, Azici, attack the enemy personnel, combat equipment and facilities." So they are ordering here that fire should be opened on the Serbian side, the troops, the combat equipment and facilities. Then they have artillery brigade observation post MPOAD [phoen], and they will place one on the cold storage plant, another one on the Brijesko Brdo, and so on. It's a document very similar to the previous one, and would you agree that, so to speak, there was not a single day in the area without any exchange of fire, and there were frequent actions and fighting which follow from such an order as this one?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: There were very frequent exchanges of fire and combat of lower and higher intensity. It's difficult to say whether it was every day, but one can certainly say that the line was never quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a word, in your mind and the mind of all people living there, the cold storage plant was hardly an economic facility, but it was rather a military facility; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this admitted, or, rather, marked for identification, because the entire document has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has already agreed to the fact that the cold plant was a military facility. Then there's no point of further examination on that point. We'll mark this for identification, pending full translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D679, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that I may as well conclude my cross-examination, and I thank Mr. Soja for meeting the Defence and for coming here to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you have any re-exam?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Just one additional question just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After the cold storage plant was unsuccessfully targeted, the system on which you worked in connection with the cold storage plant was abandoned because there was no success with targeting the cold storage plant?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the last question: You said in some statements that the AID didn't treat you quite decently; that they did not beat you, but that you were afraid, and eventually they brought you in contact with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: They conducted themselves rather professionally, but they did threaten me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just a few minutes of redirect, addressing two points that Dr. Karadzic spoke about with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The first point is the Muslims living in your settlement in Osijek. You confirmed that they left your settlement. Were they threatened, or why did they leave?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: In the place where I resided at the very beginning of the war, there were not many Muslim-populated houses, not many Muslim residents who resided there permanently. Some of them spent the entire war in Osijek, and I believe that in two instances they temporarily exchanged houses with somebody else. They moved closer to Sarajevo, and they swapped houses with some Serbs who had come from Sarajevo. In one of these cases, I know that there were some tensions, that I suppose their neighbours placed some hate phone calls. That was at the very outbreak of the war. And I was a member of the - let me call it - delegation of people who went to talk to them, and our joint conclusion was that this could be a solution, to swap houses temporarily, and that that would be the best solution possibly, because one could already see that this would turn into a serious conflict, that there would certainly be victims, and that later on it would be very difficult to guarantee safety to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the other question I have relates to your own whereabouts during the conflict. Did you participate in fighting in Otes or other places that Dr. Karadzic put to you and that were addressed in the documents?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, I practically did not directly participate in any of the fighting. It was just incidentally, and on the first day of the fighting around Otes I was re-deployed to the barracks in the rear, in Butile, and later on I was in Doglodi, but I turned up there after the main combat had already been concluded. There were sporadic exchanges of fire and shoot-outs, but I wouldn't really call it actual fighting, because I never saw a single soldier of the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you know about the planning of attacks or counter-attacks?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about military matters. But, of course, as all people from my area who were members of my unit took part in the fighting, they knew that something would be going on in the area, so I had some, let me call it, unofficial information which I learned from my neighbours and colleagues and friends that something would be taking place there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this concludes my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Soja, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Tribunal and the Bench, I would like to thank you for your coming all the way from your place to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the hearing is now adjourned until Tuesday, when we will have a hearing in the afternoon at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of October, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.20 a.m.,
